For deep_neutral_accent, the images are indeed near-monochrome (measured HSV mean saturation 0.032-0.044, mean RGB channel diffs ~1.0-1.5/255), consistent with the thumbnail's "fully monochrome" observation. However, tests/reports/phase7_background_v2/saturation_screen.json does not exist, so I built the comparison myself: I sampled 6 other deep_neutral_accent cases spanning different scenes (case_001 coastal_overlook, case_042 covered_market/centered_opening, case_082 forest_clearing, case_122 glasshouse_corridor, case_162 library_room, case_202 museum_hall, case_362 transit_concourse — 21 renders total) and computed the same mean-saturation metric. This means the near-grayscale look is how the deep_neutral_accent factor renders across the whole axis regardless of scene — it is the intended low-saturation "deep neutral" aesthetic, not a case-specific defect. case_068 is not an outlier; if anything it is slightly more saturated than the group's typical case. The thumbnail reviewer's "no color accent, real defect" call was a thumbnail-scale misread of a factor-wide, by-design characteristic — exactly the kind of thumbnail artifact the resolution protocol is meant to catch.
